Who Wins the Midterms & What It Means for Markets with Dan Clifton | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 67

Dan Clifton links midterms, tariffs, fiscal stimulus and Fed balance-sheet reform to markets. He expects a Democratic House but leans against a Senate takeover, emphasizes an underpriced data-center backlash and favors defense technology. Eisman challenges the moderate-Democrat scenario and expects a prolonged Iran conflict. Several long-term forecasts remain open; election outcomes require primary tally confirmation. The Supreme Court tariff ruling is verified, while causal macro and political explanations remain substantially unresolved.

How he reasons here

  • Use institutional control and budget leverage, not just election labels.
  • Track the change in fiscal/tariff impulse rather than gross tariff announcements.
  • Distinguish speculative motives from observable policy.
  • Treat data-center local costs and tax benefits together.
